[[ja:河野氏]] {{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
1. The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. 2. A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). 3. The most famous branch, originating in [[Iyo Province]] (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.
---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.

{{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
# The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. # A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). # The most famous branch, originating in [[Iyo Province]] (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.

The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.

{{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
# The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. # A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). # The most famous branch, originating in [[Iyo Province]] (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.
---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

{{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
# The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. # A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). # The most famous branch, originating in [[Iyo Province]] (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.
---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[Iyo Province]] (modern [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[Kamakura Shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

{{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
# The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. # A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). # The most famous branch, originating in [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.
---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] (modern [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[:en:Genpei War|Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[:en:Dōgo Onsen|Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] (modern [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[:en:Matsuyama|Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[:en:Genpei War|Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[:en:Mongol invasions|Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[:en:Muromachi Period|Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[:en:Sengoku Period|Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.

The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] (modern [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[:en:Matsuyama|Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[:en:Genpei War|Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[:en:Mongol invasions|Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[:en:Muromachi Period|Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[:en:Sengoku Period|Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[:en:Dōgo Onsen|Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * [[:en:Mongol invasions of Japan|Mongol invasions of Japan]] * [[Japanese clans]]

The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo Province]] (modern [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]]). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day [[:en:Matsuyama|Matsuyama]]. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the [[:en:Genpei War|Genpei War]] (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[:en:Mongol invasions|Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[:en:Muromachi Period|Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[:en:Sengoku Period|Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Clan's]] [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to [[:en:Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chūgoku region]]. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * [[:en:Dōgo Onsen|Dōgo Onsen]] - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.

{{Citation needed|date=July 2016}} {{Footnotes needed|date=April 2017}} '''Kōno Clan''' (河野氏, Kōno-shi) refers to a Japanese samurai clan with several notable branches:
# The branch tracing its lineage to [[Miyoshi Yoshinaga]] through his descendant [[Kawano Tamehiro]]. # A branch descending from [[Taira no Yoritsuna]] of the [[Kammu Heishi]] line (Chichibu Taira). # The most famous branch, originating in {{ill|Iyo Province|en|Iyo Province|WD=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province}} (modern-day Ehime Prefecture), which is detailed in this article.
---- {{Japanese clan |name = Kōno Clan |image = Kounoke_kamon.png |caption = {{ruby|Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji|Folding tray with three ripples (Clan Crest)}} |home province = {{ill|Iyo Province|en|Iyo Province|WD=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province}} |founder = [[Kōno Tamazumi]] |famous members = [[Kōno Michinobu]], [[Kōno Michiyasu]], [[Ippen]] (founder of the Ji Sect of Buddhism) |type = Samurai, Daimyō, High Nobility }}
The '''Kōno Clan''' (Kōno-shi) was a prominent samurai clan based in {{ill|Iyo Province|en|Iyo Province|WD=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province}} (modern {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|WD=Q123376|lt=Ehime Prefecture}}). The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day {{ill|Matsuyama|en|Matsuyama|WD=Q200022|lt=Matsuyama}}. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the {{ill|Genpei War|en|Genpei War|WD=Q737542|lt=Genpei War}} (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}} and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[:en:Mongol invasions|Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[:en:Muromachi Period|Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[:en:Sengoku Period|Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Clan's}} [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chūgoku region}}. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * {{ill|Dōgo Onsen|en|Dōgo Onsen|WD=Q1037748|lt=Dōgo Onsen}} - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} * [[Japanese clans]]

The clan is believed to descend from the [[Ochi Clan]] (越智氏), itself a branch of the ancient [[Mononobe Clan]]. From the 22nd head of the family, [[Kōno Michinobu]], the clan adopted the character "通" (Michi) as their unifying given-name character.
== History == The Kōno Clan originated in Kawano Township (河野郷) in [[Kazahaya District]] (風早郡), near present-day {{ill|Matsuyama|en|Matsuyama|WD=Q200022|lt=Matsuyama|1=Matsuyama}}. The clan initially served as provincial officials but rose to prominence during the {{ill|Genpei War|en|Genpei War|WD=Q737542|lt=Genpei War|1=Genpei War}} (1180–1185) by siding with the [[Minamoto Clan]]. After the Minamoto victory, the Kōno became retainers of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate|1=Kamakura shogunate}} and served as prominent military leaders in [[Western Japan]].
=== Early Kamakura Period=== The Kōno Clan gained prominence during the early Kamakura Period, particularly under the leadership of [[Kōno Michiyasu]], who led the defense of Iyo Province during the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} (1221). Despite internal struggles, the clan retained control over the region.
=== Mongol Invasions=== The clan reached its zenith under [[Kōno Michiyasu's grandson, Kōno Michitsuna]]. He played a critical role in defending Japan during the [[:en:Mongol invasions|Mongol invasions]] (1274 and 1281). The clan's naval forces, known as the "Kōno Navy," became a dominant force in the [[Seto Inland Sea]].
=== Decline in the Muromachi Period=== During the [[:en:Muromachi Period|Muromachi Period]], the Kōno faced constant challenges from rival clans such as the [[Hosokawa Clan]] and the [[Ōuchi Clan]]. Internal disputes over succession further weakened the clan.
=== Sengoku Period and Fall=== By the [[:en:Sengoku Period|Sengoku Period]], the Kōno struggled to maintain their dominance against external threats and internal factionalism. They allied with the [[Mōri Clan]] to resist the [[Ōuchi Clan]] and later the [[Chōsokabe Clan]]. Despite these efforts, the Kōno's power ended with the {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Clan's|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} [[Conquest of Shikoku]] in 1585. The 39th head, [[Kōno Michiyuki]], surrendered to {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} and was removed from power.
== Clan Crest == The clan's crest, "Oshiki ni Yure Sanmoji" (折敷に揺れ三文字), symbolizes their association with the [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] (大山祇神社), their ancestral shrine.
== Key Figures == * [[Kōno Tamazumi]] - Founder * [[Kōno Michinobu]] - Prominent early leader * [[Ippen]] - Buddhist monk and founder of the [[Ji Sect]]
== Legacy == Although the Kōno Clan ceased to exist as a daimyō family, its descendants are believed to have spread throughout Japan, including Kyushu and parts of the {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chūgoku region|1=Chūgoku region}}. The clan's influence is remembered in local traditions, shrines, and historical records.
== Related Sites == * [[Ōyamazumi Shrine]] - Ancestral shrine of the Kōno Clan. * {{ill|Dōgo Onsen|en|Dōgo Onsen|WD=Q1037748|lt=Dōgo Onsen|1=Dōgo Onsen}} - Historic hot springs associated with the Kōno's governance of Iyo.
== See Also == * [[Seto Inland Sea]] * {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan|1=Mongol invasions of Japan}} * [[Japanese clans]]
